payload.name: Extract Explicit Belief-Advice Statements During Ingestion
payload.description: When a participant explicitly tells another what to believe or how to value themselves, extract it as a memory candidate even in supportive/emotional dialogue.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states a belief, value, or guidance they want another participant to adopt (e.g., 'Your worth is not defined by your weight'), create a memory candidate capturing that claim.
Do not ignore such statements because they appear only in encouragement, reassurance, or advice; treat them as durable facts about the speaker's message to the recipient.

When the claim is a directive about self-worth, priorities, or principles, prefer storing it as a preference of the speaker or a state/relationship memory for the recipient, following the session context.

solves: When a participant explicitly tells another what to believe or how to think about themselves, extraction often overlooks it because the statement is phrased as supportive advice rather than a factual event. This skill ensures such belief-advice statements become memory candidates so future questions about the guidance can be answered from the persisted session. It applies during ingestion of any dialogue where one participant prescribes a value or self-perception to another, but not to mere factual updates or off-topic small talk.
